title: Precision zipper: consolidate mixed-precision kernels to eliminate dequant/requant hops
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: At decode time our current pipeline performs repeated dequant -> FP ops -> requant boundaries across attention and FFN layers, causing both token-level latency spikes and extra GPU memory traffic. Goal: Implement a 'precision zipper' approach — a consolidated mixed-precision kernel surface plus scheduler hints that keep data in INT8/FP8 lanes longer and avoid intermediate full-FP roundtrips. This reduces dequant/Requant hops, KV cache churn, and the number of memory-bound copies during prefill and streaming decode. Scope: prototype new fused attention+ffn microkernels that accept quantized KV and produce quantized outputs, runtime policy for stitching existing kernels with the new fused path, plus telemetry, fallbacks, and benchmarks across representative models (Llama2-Chat-like and instruction-tuned variants).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end streaming decode latency reduced by >= 10% p50 and 8% p99 on int8/fp8 workloads vs baseline for target models
Token-level allocator traffic (MB/s) for KV cache reduced by >= 15% in prefill-heavy workloads
No correctness regressions vs float baseline across the canonical eval set (per-token logits within tolerance) and existing unit tests pass
Graceful fallback: requests can route automatically to existing mixed-precision path if fused kernel fails or is disabled
New kernel toggles available via runtime config and surfaced in Console telemetry
implementation_notes: Design a small API shim: accept(KV_quant, attn_meta) -> produce(out_quant) to enable plugging fused kernels into existing runtime graph
Implement two kernel variants: zipper-attn-fused and zipper-attn-ffn-fused. First release will include zipper-attn-fused only to limit surface area
Use integer-friendly softmax approximation when logits remain in int8 narrow dynamic range; enable FP fallback for extreme dynamic ranges
Leverage existing quant tables and scale factors from loader to avoid extra per-request quant metadata allocation
Scheduler hint: tag prefill batches by precision lane and prefer batching tokens with identical scale tensors to avoid per-batch requantization
Memory strategy: allocate ephemeral quant buffers in a reused slab to avoid transient mallocs during streaming decode
Fallback policy: if fused path returns non-finite outputs or exceeds latency bound relative to baseline, circuit-break to legacy path and emit telemetry
test_plan: Unit tests for kernel correctness (bit-exact where applicable) and tolerance checks vs FP32 baseline
Microbenchmarks for kernel latency and memory bandwidth on target GPU instance types used by Dedicated
Integration tests: end-to-end generation with streaming enabled (short and long sequences) across int8 and fp8 quant profiles
A/B experiment: route 10% of production traffic for a canary period with blackbox metrics collection (latency, errors, token drop rate)
Regression evals: run the quality suite (prompt set) and compare generation metrics (perplexity, response divergence) to baseline
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal perf experiments on nightly clusters with synthetic traces (1 week)
Stage 2: Canary 10% on Dedicated test orgs with runtime feature flag and notebook runbook (2 weeks)
Stage 3: Ramp to 50% conditional on latency/quality gates, add console toggle for customers to opt-out
Stage 4: Default ON for new int8/fp8 model variants in runtime-2.4 if gates pass; communicate in release notes
telemetry_metrics: p50/p95/p99 token decode latency (fused vs legacy)
KV cache read/write MB/s and cache miss rate
percentage of requests using fused zipper path
token-level CPU/GPU utilization during prefill vs streaming
